text:
amy-cs: CustCorp reporting sudden p99 latency spike for /v1/generate from eu-west endpoints. reported p95 ~220ms, p99 up to 720ms since ~09:12 UTC. customer says it started after a deploy but not sure. request IDs: req_0a1b2c, req_0a1b2d
sam: grabbing traces and attn logs now. do we have a correlation with edge deploys?
oncall-bot: Deploy completed: edge-routing v2.14 at 08:57 UTC by mari-deploy (sha: a1b2c3) :deploy:
maria: I didn't touch routing rules, only smallobs to observability. but the deploy list shows edge-routing v2.14 — tagging eng-infra.
leo: I see increased SYN->ACK RTTs in eu-west pop. p50 unchanged, p95/p99 worse. starting a traceroute from pop-eu-1 to target backend cluster.
tariq: can you paste traceroute and DNS answers? also any TLS handshake failures?
sam: pasted sample request trace logs: 
```
[09:14:03] req_0a1b2c conn_id=xyz src_pop=eu-west-1 dst_pool=backend-eu-a path=[eu-pop-1 -> transitA -> us-west-2 -> transitB -> backend-eu-a]
TLS handshake time: 420ms
TCP RTT median: 18ms
Total time: 628ms
```
amy-cs: customer copy of curl timings: 600-750ms consistently for few minutes, then occasional recoveries to ~200ms. They also reported DNS returning different A records briefly.
maria: interesting, path goes via us-west-2 mid-route — looks like a hairpin cross-region hop. Could be BGP path shift or upstream transit flap.
tariq: digging into our POP routing logs: seeing increased route-preference flips at 09:11-09:13 UTC for ASN 64496 -> changed next-hop; some peers started announcing prepends. putting the raw BGP updates here: 
```
09:11:08 - peer-123: withdraw 203.0.113.0/24
09:11:12 - peer-456: announce 203.0.113.0/24 via next-hop x.x.x.x (prepended)
09:11:13 - local-pref change for path -> prefer peer-456
```
sam: So traffic rebalanced to a peer with poorer US transit, causing hairpin through us-west. That explains TLS RTT jump. do we have per-customer affinity pinned? CustCorp uses default anycast -> not pinned.
leo: Also saw DNS TTL for our egress A records at 300s. But their resolver briefly returned a US-geolocated IP due to global DNS cache state.
amy-cs: customer is sensitive to p99 for API UX. They asked for immediate mitigation.
maria: mitigation options: 1) emergency control-plane route-pin to eu-peers for their traffic (requires quick flow rule), 2) lower DNS TTL and push eu-only answers for their specific CNAME via geo steering (fast but DNS caches exist), 3) failover them to dedicated eu capacity (if enabled) to avoid anycast.
tariq: control-plane route-pin is fastest. I'll start a patch to set per-customer route-affinity for CustCorp -> prefer eu peers for 15m. need approval from oncall.
oncall-bot: oncall: @sam assigned incident-high (id: INC-8661)
sam: +1, do it. tariq, run the change and paste the commands.
tariq: running control-plane adjust: 
```
# set route-affinity for custcorp-cid 12345 -> prefer peering-set eu-primary for 15m
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/route-affinity \ 
  -d '{"cid":"12345","peer_set":"eu-primary","duration":900}' 
```
tariq: applied at 09:20:18 UTC. monitoring...
leo: metrics: p99 for CustCorp dropped to ~210ms within 40s of rule apply. overall eu-pop p99 dropped ~60% for their requests.
sam: confirm customer seeing improvement? amy-cs, ping them.
amy-cs: customer confirms latencies back to normal for last 10 mins, says they saw significant improvement. they want RCA and prevention steps.
maria: temporary mitigation successful. root cause likely upstream BGP peer path shift + DNS cache divergence leading to anycast returning non-optimal egress.
tariq: actions to prevent recurrence: - add route-preference health checks to detect and avoid peers with hairpin metrics - lower effective TTL for geo DNS answers from 300->60 for 24h during churn windows - implement per-tenant affinity opt-in for critical customers - alerting: create rule when p99_eu > 2x baseline AND cross-region hop detected
sam: also add automatic fallback to dedicated eu pool when p99>500ms for 2 minutes for customers with premium SLAs.
leo: I'll open a follow-up infra ticket with logs and BGP dumps: INFRA-4729. recommend contacting transit peer ops to understand prepends.
amy-cs: I'll send CustCorp status + ETA for RCA. include mitigation steps and offer dedicated pool for trial.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-8661 transitioned to resolved at 09:45 UTC by sam :white_check_mark:
sam: leaving notes: changed route-affinity for cust 12345 at 09:20 UTC revert scheduled at 09:50 UTC. will follow up with permanent config if infra ticket validated.
maria: agree. let's keep this incident as a reminder: anycast + upstream BGP churn can cause hairpinning even inside region. update runbook to include quick route-pin CLI snippet.
amy-cs: thanks team. I'll close customer loop and file for postmortem if infra finds transit misconfiguration.
